title: wallclock: who the waiting was for
description: Per-destination round-trip latency, measured from a send on a connection to the first bytes back on it. No thread has to block for this to be recorded, which is why it works against a Go service. Point the exporter at one cgroup -- `wallclock destinations -cgroup ... -serve :9500` -- or every connection on the machine ends up here.

panels.title: p99 round trip, by destination
panels.description: histogram_quantile over the buckets, which are ceilings with four buckets to the octave -- so a value is 'at or below', never an interpolation. Restricted to destinations doing more than one exchange a second: below that the interval measured is a peer's think time rather than a round trip, and one idle keep-alive at two minutes flattens every real series to zero.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (name, destination, le) (rate(wallclock_destination_latency_seconds_bucket[1m]))) and on (destination) (sum by (destination) (rate(wallclock_destination_latency_seconds_count[1m])) > 1)

panels.title: mean round trip, by destination
panels.description: Sum over count, so this one is exact rather than read off the histogram. Same traffic floor as the p99 panel.

targets.expr: (sum by (name, destination) (rate(wallclock_destination_latency_seconds_sum[1m])) / sum by (name, destination) (rate(wallclock_destination_latency_seconds_count[1m]))) and on (destination) (sum by (destination) (rate(wallclock_destination_latency_seconds_count[1m])) > 1)

panels.title: completed exchanges per second
panels.description: How much conversation there is with each peer. A destination with a high latency and two exchanges a second is a different problem from one with a low latency and ten thousand -- which is why this panel is unfiltered.
